companions.why: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.

Chip select is active low and shared with whatever else sits on the bus. Held high while the host is in reset, the device ignores the bus; floating, it answers noise as though it were a command — and on a writable device that is a corrupted cell rather than a bad read.

rules.why: A supply or return pin that reaches no net means the part is unpowered.
Two drivers on one net fight; whichever is stronger sources the other's short-circuit current.
An output tied straight to a supply or ground is a short the moment it drives the other way.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.

A series resistor at the oscillator damps the clock trace so its own reflection does not double-clock the receiver. It is a transmission-line remedy rather than a functional requirement, so it warns.

rules.why: A supply or return pin that reaches no net means the part is unpowered.
Two drivers on one net fight; whichever is stronger sources the other's short-circuit current.
An output tied straight to a supply or ground is a short the moment it drives the other way.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.

An output tied straight to a supply or ground is a short the moment it drives the other way.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
An open-drain pin can only pull down; without a pull-up its net never reaches a logic high.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.

companions.why: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.

An RF stage draws in bursts as the transmitter keys. The 100nF at each supply pin answers the fast edge and is far too small to hold the rail through a burst; the bulk capacitor is what stops the supply sagging mid-packet.

A capacitor on reset stretches the release past the supply's rise and keeps noise off the pin.
Reset needs a defined idle level. Many parts have an internal pull-up, which is why this is a warning rather than an error.
The radio draws hundreds of milliamps in bursts. A rail without real bulk capacitance browns out on the first transmit and the part resets.
EN must be high for the part to run at all, and it has no internal pull-up.
The RC on EN delays release until the supply is up, which is what makes cold starts reliable.

The radio draws hundreds of milliamps in bursts. A rail without real bulk capacitance browns out on the first transmit and the part resets.
EN must be high for the part to run at all, and it has no internal pull-up.
The RC on EN delays release until the supply is up, which is what makes cold starts reliable.

An RF stage draws in bursts as the transmitter keys. The 100nF at each supply pin answers the fast edge and is far too small to hold the rail through a burst; the bulk capacitor is what stops the supply sagging mid-packet.

An output tied straight to a supply or ground is a short the moment it drives the other way.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.

companions.why: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.

An output tied straight to a supply or ground is a short the moment it drives the other way.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.

companions.why: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.
The input capacitor carries the switching current. Placed far away, or absent, the input rail carries it instead and the whole board sees the ripple.
The output capacitor turns the inductor's triangular current into a usable rail and closes the loop.
